```{r, include=FALSE}
library(openxlsx, quietly = TRUE, warn.conflicts = FALSE)
library(tidyverse, quietly = TRUE, warn.conflicts = FALSE)
library(knitr, quietly = TRUE, warn.conflicts = FALSE)
library(dplyr, quietly = TRUE, warn.conflicts = FALSE)
library(MASS)

bi_freq <- read.xlsx("srcsc-2026-claims-business-interruption.xlsx",sheet=1)
bi_sev <- read.xlsx("srcsc-2026-claims-business-interruption.xlsx",sheet=2)
bi_freq$solar_system <- gsub("_.*","",bi_freq$solar_system)
bi_sev$solar_system <- gsub("_.*","",bi_sev$solar_system)


bi_freq <- bi_freq %>% 
  filter(production_load <=1,
         production_load >=0,
         energy_backup_score %in% c(1,2,3,4,5),
         supply_chain_index <=1,
         supply_chain_index >=0,
         avg_crew_exp <=30,
         avg_crew_exp >= 1,
         maintenance_freq <= 6,
         maintenance_freq >= 0,
         safety_compliance %in% c(1,2,3,4,5),
         claim_count <= 4,
         claim_count >=0)

bi_sev <- bi_sev %>% 
  filter(production_load <=1,
         production_load >=0,
         energy_backup_score %in% c(1,2,3,4,5),
         safety_compliance %in% c(1,2,3,4,5),
         claim_amount <= 150000000,
         claim_amount >= 25000)


bi_pol <- bi_freq %>%
  filter(!is.na(exposure), !is.na(claim_count), exposure > 0, !is.na(solar_system)) %>%
  group_by(policy_id) %>%
  summarise(
    exposure_pol = sum(exposure, na.rm = TRUE),
    claims_pol   = sum(claim_count, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(exposure_pol > 0)

bi_risk_lookup <- bi_freq %>%
  group_by(policy_id) %>%
  summarise(
    supply_chain_index = mean(supply_chain_index, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_crew_exp       = mean(avg_crew_exp, na.rm = TRUE),
    production_load    = mean(production_load, na.rm = TRUE),
    energy_backup_score= mean(energy_backup_score, na.rm = TRUE),
    maintenance_freq   = mean(maintenance_freq, na.rm = TRUE),
    safety_compliance  = mean(safety_compliance, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# 2. Before joining, remove the duplicate columns from bi_sev 
# so the new ones from the lookup take their place without the .x or .y suffix
bi_sev_cleaned <- bi_sev %>% 
  dplyr::select(-one_of(intersect(names(bi_sev), names(bi_risk_lookup)[names(bi_risk_lookup) != "policy_id"]))) %>%
  left_join(bi_risk_lookup, by = "policy_id")
```

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
lambda_hat <- sum(bi_pol$claims_pol) / sum(bi_pol$exposure_pol)
lambda_hat

mean_claims <- mean(bi_pol$claims_pol)
var_claims  <- var(bi_pol$claims_pol)

dispersion_ratio <- var_claims / mean_claims
c(mean_claims = mean_claims, var_claims = var_claims, dispersion_ratio = dispersion_ratio)
```

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
x <- bi_sev$claim_amount
x <- as.numeric(x)
x <- x[is.finite(x) & !is.na(x) & x > 0]

mu    <- mean(log(x))
sigma <- sd(log(x))

mean_sev   <- exp(mu + 0.5*sigma^2)
median_sev <- exp(mu)

c(meanlog = mu, sdlog = sigma, mean_severity = mean_sev, median_severity = median_sev)
```

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
hist(
  log(x),
  breaks = 50,
  main = "Log of Business Interruption Amounts",
  xlab = "log(Claim Amount)"
)

p<- qqplot(
  qlnorm(ppoints(length(x)), meanlog = mu, sdlog = sigma),
  sort(x),
  main = "QQ Plot – Cargo Severity (Lognormal)",
  xlab = "Theoretical Quantiles",
  ylab = "Observed Claim Amounts"
) 
abline(0, 1, col = "red", lwd = 2)
```

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
loglik_logn <- sum(dlnorm(x, meanlog = mu, sdlog = sigma, log = TRUE))
aic_logn <- 2*2 - 2*loglik_logn

m <- mean(x); v <- var(x)
shape_hat <- m^2 / v
rate_hat  <- m / v

loglik_gam <- sum(dgamma(x, shape = shape_hat, rate = rate_hat, log = TRUE))
aic_gam <- 2*2 - 2*loglik_gam

data.frame(
  Model = c("Lognormal", "Gamma"),
  AIC   = c(aic_logn, aic_gam),
  row.names = NULL
)
```

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
q95 <- qlnorm(0.95, meanlog = mu, sdlog = sigma)
q99 <- qlnorm(0.99, meanlog = mu, sdlog = sigma)

c(q95_logn = q95, q99_logn = q99)

quantile(x, probs = c(0.90, 0.95, 0.99))
mean(x)
```

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
delta_aic <- aic_gam - aic_logn

cat(
  "- **Baseline frequency (lambda_hat):** ", round(lambda_hat, 4), " claims per exposure-year\n",
  "- **Overdispersion (Var/Mean):** ", round(dispersion_ratio, 3), " → Negative Binomial preferred\n",
  "- **Severity model:** Lognormal (meanlog = ", round(mu, 3), ", sdlog = ", round(sigma, 3), ")\n",
  "- **Mean severity (Lognormal):** $", format(round(mean_sev, 0), big.mark=","), "\n",
  "- **AIC comparison (Gamma - Lognormal):** ΔAIC = ", round(delta_aic, 1), " (positive favors Lognormal)\n",
  sep = ""
)
```

## PART TWOOOOOOO

```{r}

# Start by getting parameters for the distribution you chose for your claim freq count. (Either Poisson or NB) I will be doing it for NB since that's what i chose in Part 1. 
bi_pol <- bi_pol %>%
  left_join(bi_risk_lookup, by = "policy_id")
# Finding my parameters while taking into account exposure!! NegBin with exposure offset: E[claims | exposure] = rate * exposure. Also just as a side note in the traditional NB we use (r,p), in this case we are setting r = theta and p = theta/(theta+mu). This is common practice in actuarial pricing. 
fit_nb <- glm.nb(claims_pol ~ production_load + energy_backup_score + 
                 supply_chain_index + avg_crew_exp + maintenance_freq + 
                 safety_compliance + offset(log(exposure_pol)), 
                 data = bi_pol)
summary(fit_nb)

# After you fit the model you can now find the actual parameters.
lambda_hat_nb <- exp(coef(fit_nb)[1])  
# lamba is rate per exposure unit
theta_nb      <- fit_nb$theta           
#  theta is the dispersion parameter AKA our (p) parameter

c(lambda_hat_nb = lambda_hat_nb, theta_nb = theta_nb)

```

## Time to use your severity and freq distributions to run some simulations!! We are using these simulations to see what the expected losses will be on average in the worst stress years as well as the worst 1% of years. (This is what Var and TVaR is)

```{r}

# you must start by setting your exposure period which is the sum of your exposure

total_exposure <- sum(bi_pol$exposure_pol)

Exposure_period <- total_exposure 

mu_period <- as.numeric(lambda_hat_nb) * Exposure_period
mu_period

# this is the expected/theoretical mean that we are shooting for. We will use this number to compare to the simulated mean

expected_aggregate <- as.numeric(lambda_hat_nb) * Exposure_period * mean_sev
expected_aggregate

# SIMULATION TIME YAYYYY - i stole bootstrapping code from 424

set.seed(123)
n_sims <- 30000

mu_period <- as.numeric(lambda_hat_nb) * Exposure_period

agg_losses <- numeric(n_sims)

for (i in seq_len(n_sims)) {
  N <- rnbinom(1, size = theta_nb, mu = mu_period)
  if (N == 0) {
    agg_losses[i] <- 0
  } else {
    agg_losses[i] <- sum(rlnorm(N, meanlog = mu, sdlog = sigma))
  }
}

# these are the values we will be putting in a table that we want

mean_L  <- mean(agg_losses)
VaR_99  <- as.numeric(quantile(agg_losses, 0.99, names = FALSE))
TVaR_99 <- mean(agg_losses[agg_losses >= VaR_99])

# in the table below you'll notice my ratio is super close to 1 this is AWESOME and means the simulation is correct.

c(sim_mean = mean_L, theo_mean = expected_aggregate, ratio = mean_L/expected_aggregate,
  VaR_99 = VaR_99, TVaR_99 = TVaR_99)

```

## Fitting models/simulation for each solar system

```{r}

# find the biggest risks from each solar system that DIRECTLY effect your specific hazard. For example for Cargo debris density obvi effects cargo collisions, so when reading about each system I saw that Heli had the most debris so i put it in the .95 quantile compared to the other solar systems.


#Also on the lowest of keys i gave chat info about each of the solar systems and 

# Solar System, Production Load, Energy Backup Score,
# Supply Chain Index, Average Crew Experience, Maintenance
# Frequency, Safety Compliance

q <- function(v, p) as.numeric(quantile(v, p, na.rm = TRUE))

profiles <- rbind(
  Helionis = data.frame(
    production_load       = q(bi_freq$production_load, 0.99),
    energy_backup_score   = q(bi_freq$energy_backup_score, 0.30),
    supply_chain_index    = q(bi_freq$supply_chain_index , 0.65),
    avg_crew_exp          = q(bi_freq$avg_crew_exp  , 0.85),

  ),
  Bayesia = data.frame(
    production_load       = q(bi_freq$production_load, 0.67),
    energy_backup_score   = q(bi_freq$energy_backup_score, 0.55),
    supply_chain_index    = q(bi_freq$supply_chain_index , 0.90),
    avg_crew_exp          = q(bi_freq$avg_crew_exp  , 0.70),
    maintenance_freq      = q(bi_freq$maintenance_freq, 0.60),
    safety_compliance     = q(bi_freq$safety_compliance,0.8),
    exposure_pol          = 1
  ),
  Oryn = data.frame(
    production_load       = q(bi_freq$production_load, 0.33),
    energy_backup_score   = q(bi_freq$energy_backup_score, 0.90),
    supply_chain_index    = q(bi_freq$supply_chain_index , 0.45),
    avg_crew_exp          = q(bi_freq$avg_crew_exp  , 0.40),
    maintenance_freq      = q(bi_freq$maintenance_freq, 0.50),
    safety_compliance     = q(bi_freq$safety_compliance,0.95),
    exposure_pol          = 1
  )
)

profiles

```

```{r}
# baseline profile = "typical" environment
baseline <- data.frame(
    # Pulling medians from bi_freq ensures the columns exist
    production_load       = median(bi_freq$production_load, na.rm=TRUE),
    energy_backup_score   = median(bi_freq$energy_backup_score, na.rm=TRUE),
    supply_chain_index    = median(bi_freq$supply_chain_index , na.rm=TRUE),
    avg_crew_exp          = median(bi_freq$avg_crew_exp  , na.rm=TRUE),
    maintenance_freq      = median(bi_freq$maintenance_freq, na.rm=TRUE),
    safety_compliance     = median(bi_freq$safety_compliance, na.rm=TRUE),
    exposure_pol          = 1
)

# Frequency (claims per exposure unit)
freq_base <- as.numeric(predict(fit_nb, newdata = baseline,  type = "response"))
freq_sys  <- as.numeric(predict(fit_nb, newdata = profiles, type = "response"))

freq_mult <- freq_sys / freq_base
names(freq_mult) <- rownames(profiles)
freq_mult


# Create a unique lookup table of policy attributes first
# 1. Create the lookup table with the unique columns you need
bi_risk_lookup <- bi_freq %>%
  group_by(policy_id) %>%
  summarise(
    supply_chain_index = mean(supply_chain_index, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_crew_exp       = mean(avg_crew_exp, na.rm = TRUE),
    production_load    = mean(production_load, na.rm = TRUE),
    energy_backup_score= mean(energy_backup_score, na.rm = TRUE),
    maintenance_freq   = mean(maintenance_freq, na.rm = TRUE),
    safety_compliance  = mean(safety_compliance, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# 2. Before joining, remove the duplicate columns from bi_sev 
# so the new ones from the lookup take their place without the .x or .y suffix
bi_sev_cleaned <- bi_sev %>% 
  dplyr::select(-one_of(intersect(names(bi_sev), names(bi_risk_lookup)[names(bi_risk_lookup) != "policy_id"]))) %>%
  left_join(bi_risk_lookup, by = "policy_id")

# 3. Now fit the model - the names will match exactly
fit_sev <- glm(log(claim_amount) ~ production_load + energy_backup_score + 
               supply_chain_index + avg_crew_exp + maintenance_freq + 
               safety_compliance, 
               data = bi_sev_cleaned)

# 2. Predict baseline (median of all data)
log_m_base <- as.numeric(predict(fit_sev, newdata = baseline))

# 3. Predict for our specific Solar Systems
log_m_sys  <- as.numeric(predict(fit_sev, newdata = profiles))

# 4. Calculate the Multipliers
sev_mult <- exp(log_m_sys - log_m_base)
names(sev_mult) <- rownames(profiles)

sev_mult


```

```{r}

simulate_system <- function(E_period, f_mult, s_mult, n_sims = 30000, seed = 123) {
  set.seed(seed)
  
  # Ensure we are working with clean numbers, not named vectors
  f_mult <- as.numeric(f_mult)
  s_mult <- as.numeric(s_mult)
  
  # Calculate the expected number of claims for the period
  # lambda_hat_nb should be your baseline frequency from the NB model
  mu_period <- as.numeric(lambda_hat_nb) * f_mult * E_period

  # Step 1: Generate N (number of claims) for all simulations at once
  # This is much faster than a for-loop
  N_sims <- rnbinom(n_sims, size = theta_nb, mu = mu_period)
  
  # Step 2: Generate aggregate losses
  agg <- sapply(N_sims, function(n) {
    if (n == 0) return(0)
    # Applying the severity multiplier to the meanlog
    sum(rlnorm(n, meanlog = mu + log(s_mult), sdlog = sigma))
  })

  # Step 3: Calculate Metrics
  VaR_99  <- quantile(agg, 0.99, names = FALSE)
  TVaR_99 <- mean(agg[agg >= VaR_99])

  c(E_L = mean(agg), Var_L = var(agg), VaR_99 = VaR_99, TVaR_99 = TVaR_99)
}
E_total <- total_exposure
# Run the simulation
out <- rbind(
  Helionis = simulate_system(E_total, freq_mult["Helionis"], sev_mult["Helionis"]),
  Bayesia  = simulate_system(E_total, freq_mult["Bayesia"],  sev_mult["Bayesia"]),
  Oryn     = simulate_system(E_total, freq_mult["Oryn"],     sev_mult["Oryn"])
)

print(out)


```
